page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.24xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the ARM64 architecture. It features 96 dedicated physical cores utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or GPU hardware. Network connectivity is a key feature, delivering a baseline bandwidth of 300 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with cached read-only speeds reaching 11,079.27 GB/sec and uncached write speeds at 240.83 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category. The server excels in database operations, showing top-tier results in Redis SET operations and PassMark database tests, alongside strong static web serving throughput.

The ARM-based architecture offers high resource density and multi-core efficiency, making it a cost-effective option for highly parallelized workloads. The primary tradeoff is the lack of local NVMe storage, meaning all storage operations must rely on network-attached EBS volumes, though this is mitigated by the high baseline network bandwidth. The server is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, database hosting, static web serving, software compilation, and medium-to-large scale LLM text generation.
